causes.text: Apple delayed the production ramp-up of its 2020 flagship iPhones by about a month amid pandemic disruptions.

source_info.title: Apple to delay mass production of 2020 flagship iPhones

effects.text: Broadcom indicated the annual iPhone-related chip shipment ramp would occur one quarter later than usual.

source_info.title: Broadcom signals delay in iPhone chip ramp-up, pointing to later release date

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Apple's 2020 iPhone mass-production ramp was pushed back by about one month due to COVID-19 disruptions, indicating a later-than-usual launch window for the cycle.

Because Apple is a major downstream demand driver-and accounted for roughly one-fifth of Broadcom's 2019 revenue-the slip in Apple's schedule shifted suppliers' shipment seasonality by one quarter (from the typical late Q3 ramp toward Q4), reducing near-term order visibility and cash collection.
On Sep 3, 2020, Broadcom said its annual iPhone-related chip ramp would run into the final calendar quarter (about one quarter later than most years) and guided fiscal Q4 revenue to about $6.4B.
Market reaction: Broadcom (AVGO) shares rose about 1.7% in extended trading on Sep 3, 2020 following the update and guidance.

rationale: Reuters linked the iPhone production delay to Broadcom's later ramp commentary, aligning supplier seasonality with Apple's shifted schedule.
counterfactual_analysis: If iPhone production had proceeded on the usual timeline, Broadcom's wireless revenue ramp would likely have occurred a quarter earlier.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Could independently delay component shipments regardless of Apple's schedule.

details.commentary: Apple's decision to delay its iPhone launch shifts Broadcom's usual shipment ramp into a later quarter, creating a temporary dip followed by a catch-up in orders. That timing shift smooths out over the product cycle, but it still changes the quarterly revenue profile enough for investors to adjust near-term expectations.
